name: aphid
description: Insect pest (Rhopalosiphum padi / Sitobion avenae) and viral vector affecting foliage and sap.
causes: Colonization by Rhopalosiphum padi / Sitobion avenae under warm conditions.
treatment: Apply recommended systemic insecticide (e.g., imidacloprid)
Encourage beneficial predator populations such as ladybirds
Monitor field margins regularly

name: black-rust
description: Stem rust caused by Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici, an airborne Basidiomycete with epidemic potential.
symptoms: Dark reddish-brown to black elongated pustules on stems and leaf sheaths
causes: Windborne urediniospores of Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici spreading in warm, moist weather.
treatment: Apply triazole or strobilurin fungicides (e.g., tebuconazole)
Sow resistant wheat cultivars
Eradicate alternate host barberry bushes

name: blast
description: Severe spike infection caused by Magnaporthe oryzae Triticum pathotype.
symptoms: Completely bleached spikes while canopy remains green
causes: Airborne conidia and infected seeds under warm, wet conditions during flowering.
treatment: Prophylactic fungicide spray at heading and early flowering
Use certified disease-free seed
Enforce regional quarantine protocols

name: brown-rust
description: Leaf rust caused by Puccinia triticina, reducing green photosynthetic leaf area.
symptoms: Small circular to oval orange-brown pustules scattered across upper leaf surfaces
causes: Windborne spores of Puccinia triticina favored by mild temperatures and dew.
treatment: Foliar fungicide application (propiconazole, tebuconazole)
Plant cultivars carrying effective Lr resistance genes

name: common-root-rot
description: Soil- and seed-borne root and crown rot caused by Bipolaris sorokiniana.
symptoms: Dark brown to black subcrown lesions
causes: Soil inoculum and infected seed surviving in dry, compacted soils.
treatment: Fungicidal seed treatment
Rotate with non-cereal crops such as legumes or oilseeds
Maintain balanced soil phosphorus and potassium

name: flag-smut
description: Systemic fungal disease caused by Urocystis agropyri producing dark spore streaks on leaves.
symptoms: Long gray-black stripes on flag leaves
causes: Seed-borne and soil-borne teliospores persisting in soil.
treatment: Seed dressing with carboxin or tebuconazole
Deep summer tillage
Crop rotation

name: fusarium-head-blight
description: Head blight caused by Fusarium graminearum, causing mycotoxin (deoxynivalenol/DON) accumulation.
symptoms: Orange/pink spore masses along glume margins
causes: Rain-splash and windborne ascospores from maize and cereal residues during anthesis.
treatment: Targeted triazole fungicide (prothioconazole or metconazole) at early flowering
Avoid direct maize-to-wheat rotation
Choose moderately resistant cultivars

name: healthy
description: Asymptomatic, healthy Triticum aestivum crop canopy with vigorous growth.
symptoms: Absence of chlorotic or necrotic lesions
causes: Proper agronomic management and absence of pathogen infection.
treatment: Maintain recommended irrigation and balanced nutrition
Periodic scouting for early pest/disease detection

name: leaf-blight
description: Foliar blight caused by Bipolaris sorokiniana and Alternaria triticina complex.
symptoms: Small brown oval lesions expanding into irregular necrotic patches with yellow halos
causes: Warm temperatures (20-25 C) combined with high relative humidity.
treatment: Foliar spray with mancozeb or propiconazole at symptom onset
Field sanitation and destruction of volunteer crops

name: mildew
description: Biotrophic foliar infection caused by Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici.
symptoms: White to grayish powdery colonies on upper leaf surfaces and stems
causes: Airborne conidia favored by dense canopy shade, high nitrogen, and cool humid conditions.
treatment: Apply sulfur-based or triazole fungicides
Optimize nitrogen dosage to prevent succulent canopy
Ensure proper plant spacing for canopy ventilation

name: mite
description: Microscopic arachnid pest (Aceria tosichella) and primary vector for Wheat Streak Mosaic Virus.
causes: Wind dispersal of mites from volunteer wheat and wild grasses.
treatment: Eliminate volunteer wheat at least 2 weeks before sowing to break green bridge
Delay autumn sowing
Select mite-resistant cultivars

name: septoria
description: Necrotrophic foliar disease caused by Zymoseptoria tritici.
symptoms: Irregular brown necrotic lesions bounded by leaf veins
Prominent black speckles (pycnidia) embedded in necrotic lesions
causes: Rain-splashed pycnidiospores moving upwards from lower canopy in wet conditions.
treatment: Apply protective or early curative fungicides (SDHI, triazole mixtures)
Incorporate crop stubble
Crop rotation

name: stem-fly
description: Stem boring insect pest (Atherigona oryzae / Cephus cinctus) causing deadheart symptoms.
symptoms: Central tiller shoot drying and turning pale (deadheart)
Internal tunneling and frass in stems
causes: Egg laying by adult flies followed by larval tunneling into growing points.
treatment: Adjust sowing date to avoid peak fly activity
Seed treatment with approved systemic insecticides
Destroy harvested stubble

name: tan-spot
description: Foliar disease caused by Pyrenophora tritici-repentis.
symptoms: Tan oval lesions with a dark central spot and distinct yellow halo
Coalescing lesions causing blighting of upper leaves
causes: Ascospores released from wheat stubble residues during moist spring weather.
treatment: Foliar fungicide application at flag leaf emergence
Rotate crops away from wheat for at least one season
Residue management

name: yellow-rust
description: Stripe rust caused by Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici, forming parallel stripes of bright yellow uredinia.
symptoms: Bright yellow pustules aligned in distinctive linear stripes along leaf veins
Chlorosis and drying of infected leaves
causes: Airborne transport of urediniospores under cool (10-15 C) and humid conditions.
treatment: Prompt foliar application of triazole fungicides (propiconazole, tebuconazole)
Deploy resistant varieties carrying Yr resistance genes
